SABLE_01.speaker: Guildmaster Sable [via Starlight Raven]
SABLE_01.text: So. The skiff shattered on the crag reefs, just as I calculated. No matter, Voss. A thief who requires a return ticket is a thief with one foot in the grave. Look up at that mountain.

choices.text: The fortress looks dead, Sable. Not a sentry on the parapet.
My contract was to steal the child's music box, not breach a fortified citadel on foot.
[Examine the glowing purple brambles blocking the stairs]

SABLE_02A.speaker: Guildmaster Sable [via Starlight Raven]
SABLE_02A.text: Dead? Veilkeep hasn't died in eighty winters—it has merely forgotten how to rot. Vaelor's wards hold the entire crag in an eternal, breathing dream. Walk softly, Kaelen. Step on the wrong cobblestone and the house will wake.

choices.text: Where do I start?

SABLE_02B.speaker: Guildmaster Sable [via Starlight Raven]
SABLE_02B.text: The music box IS the citadel, Voss. That broken cylinder holds the harmonic resonance frequency that pins Vaelor's entire illusion to the world. Retrieve Cynthia's seven shards, and the Master's palace folds like paper. Three thousand silver moons upon delivery.

choices.text: Understood. What of the courtyard obstacles?

SABLE_02C.speaker: Guildmaster Sable [via Starlight Raven]
SABLE_02C.text: Sharp eye, Master Voss. Aether-bramble. Thrives in dark mists, chokes on starlight and fire. Un-shutter the terrace oil-reflectors. Flood the staircase with warm beam-light, and the vines will retreat like scalded serpents.

choices.text: I will clear the path.

SABLE_03.speaker: Guildmaster Sable [via Starlight Raven]
SABLE_03.text: Infiltrate the sunken courtyard. Seek out Gatekeeper Orin at the portcullis; the guild has slipped a doubt into his mind. Strike hard, steal true, and never look into a mirror you did not bring yourself.

choices.text: [Dismiss the raven and draw Whisper]

ORIN_01.speaker: Gatekeeper Orin
ORIN_01.text: Hold! In the name of... who was the Duke again? Why can't I remember the color of my sister's hair? Stranger... stand back! My halberd is steel. It is steel, isn't it?

choices.text: Lower the blade, soldier. You are bleeding violet light.
[Strike an Iron Nail into the gatehouse oak table]
You're an automaton, sentry. Step aside before I dismantle your spring.

ORIN_02A.speaker: Gatekeeper Orin
ORIN_02A.text: Light... cold starlight. For forty years I stood on this flagstone, believing my relief watch was arriving at dawn. But dawn never comes. If you cut me, will I leave an echo or a corpse?

choices.text: You are real enough to think, Orin. Let me anchor you with an Iron Nail.
Give me the Gatehouse Key. I will ascend the spire and make Vaelor answer.

ORIN_GROUNDED.speaker: Gatekeeper Orin
ORIN_GROUNDED.text: Ah... cold iron. The weight... the gravity of it. My mother's stove was forged of iron. My name is Orin of the Lower Mill. The Master's spell... it shattered in my skull!

choices.text: Take this nail and hold the threshold, Orin. How do I enter the Servants' Hall?

ORIN_REWARD.speaker: Gatekeeper Orin
ORIN_REWARD.text: Take the Gatehouse Key. But heed this: the main corridor is monitored by the Warden's mirrors. Take the scullery dumbwaiter behind Cook Hesta's ovens. And tell Cynthia... Orin remembered to lock the outer gate.

choices.text: [Take Gatehouse Key and enter Servants' Quarters]

ORIN_COMBAT.speaker: Gatekeeper Orin
ORIN_COMBAT.text: Alarm! Intruders in the outer gatehouse! By the Archillusionist's decree, none shall pass!

choices.text: [Draw weapon and defend yourself]

BART_01.speaker: Mister Bartholomew Sterling
BART_01.text: Good evening, sir. If you intend to burgle the household silver, you will find the spoons to the left and the fish knives to the right. However, house regulations strictly prohibit cold steel at the breakfast table. Do kindly sheathe that dagger before the Duchess notices.

choices.text: [Sheathe Whisper and bow with formal decorum]
The Duchess has been dead for eighty years, Sterling. There is no breakfast.
Hand over the household master passkey, old man, or I'll take it.

BART_02A.speaker: Mister Bartholomew Sterling
BART_02A.text: Exquisite deportment, Master Voss. A gentleman may find himself in the employ of shadows, but he never neglects his saucer. The late Duchess always maintained that good manners are the only barrier between civilization and the abyss.

choices.text: You know my name, Mister Sterling?
I came seeking Cynthia's memory shards.

BART_02B.speaker: Mister Bartholomew Sterling
BART_02B.text: A vulgar rumor spread by illiterate footmen, sir. The Duchess is merely delayed in the conservatory. And young Lady Cynthia is taking her afternoon rest. Until the Master rings the bronze bell, service continues.

choices.text: Forgive my bluntness. Let me assist with the household service.

BART_02C.speaker: Mister Bartholomew Sterling
BART_02C.text: Threats at the tea table? How dreadfully provincial. You may strike down this tired shade, Master Voss, but you will search forty thousand cupboards without the proper brass sequence.

choices.text: [Lower weapon] My apologies, Mister Sterling. How can I earn the key?

BART_CYNTHIA.speaker: Mister Bartholomew Sterling
BART_CYNTHIA.text: Young Lady Cynthia... she was fond of hiding beneath the linen baskets when you were a boy, Master Voss. She told me once: 'Kaelen will become the greatest thief in the world, and then he will come back and steal me away from father's clockwork.' It appears she was half-right. You returned.

choices.text: Help me reach her, Bartholomew.

BART_QUEST_OFFER.speaker: Mister Bartholomew Sterling
BART_QUEST_OFFER.text: The brigands who ransacked the south pantry made off with the Duchess's Sterling Teapot, and young Cynthia's porcelain cup was taken to the Playhouse green room. Recover them. Execute the three-point afternoon tea service for Doctor Renatus, Maestro Niccolò, and Lady Eleanor. Do this, and the Grand Seneschal's Master Passkey to all twenty-seven fortress zones is yours.

choices.text: I accept the service, Mister Sterling.

ELDRIN_01.speaker: Eldrin the Star-Carver
ELDRIN_01.text: Step no closer... shadow-walker. The floor... is tethered to the Warden's dynamo. Every breath I draw feeds the siphon... holding the deep dark back from the keep.

choices.text: I solved the siphon valves, Eldrin. The cage is grounded. I am getting you out.
Hold on, old man! Drink this Aether Tonic!

ELDRIN_SACRIFICE.speaker: Eldrin the Star-Carver
ELDRIN_SACRIFICE.text: Look at my hands, boy. There is no flesh left to rescue. Vaelor carved out my heart forty years ago to power his mirror stars. Take it! Take the last ember of the Star-Carvers! When you walk through the Master's deepest shadow, let this light burn his mirrors to ash!

choices.text: [Grip Eldrin's hand as the light converges into the amulet]

MAREN_01.speaker: Librarian Maren
MAREN_01.text: Silence, intruder. The dust on these shelves has ears, and Vaelor's censors listen through the ventilation flues. If you seek gold, the treasury is east. If you seek the truth of the plague year... you have brought an inadequate dagger.

choices.text: I seek Cynthia's true history, Maren. Why is her name struck from every ledger?
[Present the red-ink diary page recovered from the Nursery]

MAREN_02.speaker: Librarian Maren
MAREN_02.text: Cynthia did not die of the autumn plague. She died of Vaelor's experiments with reverse-entropy mirrors. And when her heart stopped, his mind shattered. Reorder the six suppressed annals, and I will give you the Memory Thread to navigate the shifting corridors upstairs.

choices.text: I will restore the true timeline.

ELEANOR_01.speaker: Lady Eleanor the Sun-Scarred
ELEANOR_01.text: You tread softly, child of shadow. Are you another of Vaelor's phantasms sent to mimic the confession of my fallen knights?

choices.text: No phantom, Lady Eleanor. I am Kaelen Voss.
Sir Roderick still stands on the high solarium. He is calcified in stone.

ELEANOR_02.speaker: Lady Eleanor the Sun-Scarred
ELEANOR_02.text: The Solar Prism atop this altar is blinded with mirror grime. Cleanse the four pedestal mirrors with Consecration Oil. Align them to the virtues of dawn: Justice, Fortitude, Temperance, Truth. Converge the pure sunlight into the monstrance, and shatter the curse binding Roderick!

choices.text: I will ignite the sun upon your altar, Lady Eleanor.

AURELIUS_01.speaker: Lord Aurelius the Sky-Sovereign
AURELIUS_01.text: Crawl no closer, mortal mite! For two hundred years the Archillusionist has caged my roost with humming clockwork wind-baffles and stolen the Solar Heart to power his false storm! Do you come with a butcher's blade or an executioner's bell?

choices.text: I come with neither, Sovereign. I came to shatter your shackles.
[Ring the Echo Bell to harmonize with his scream]

AURELIUS_PACT.speaker: Lord Aurelius the Sky-Sovereign
AURELIUS_PACT.text: Boreas in C, Eurus in G, Notus in C, Zephyrus in E! Align the steam sliders to the celestial octave! Bring me the Solar Heart, and I will sweep Vaelor's false clouds from the sky! Wrap my golden mantle around your shoulders—take to the air!

choices.text: The sky shall be yours again, Sovereign.

ASTERION_STUN.speaker: Asterion the Brass-Horned
ASTERION_STUN.text: The maze... the roaring in my skull... make it stop! Mother... where is the thread? I cannot see the sky... only brass... only blood!

choices.text: [Use Whisper to sever the steam-control collar at his nape]
[Drive Daybreak into his exposed steam core]

ASTERION_FREED.speaker: Asterion the Liberated
ASTERION_FREED.text: The roaring... it has ceased. For seventy winters Vaelor made me his brute, burying my compass in iron. You held the thread, shadow-walker. Take my labrys—when you stand before the deceiver, let him hear the brass horns of the labyrinth!

choices.text: Rest now, Asterion. The labyrinth is open.

ASTERION_SLAIN.speaker: Asterion the Slain
ASTERION_SLAIN.text: *(With a final shuddering groan of scalding steam, the minotaur collapses; the brass labrys slips from his dying grip)*

choices.text: [Retrieve the Labrys and Horn from the steam]

VAELOR_01.speaker: Archillusionist Vaelor
VAELOR_01.text: Kaelen. My little thief. Eighty years I watched you in the glass, waiting to see if the world beyond my walls had learned to conquer death. And what did you bring me? Cold iron. Severed threads. The screams of my servants.

choices.text: I brought the truth, Vaelor. Lower the veil. Cynthia is gone.
You didn't build this keep to protect her. You built it because you couldn't face an empty room.
[Hold up the completed Shattered Glass Music Box]

VAELOR_02A.speaker: Archillusionist Vaelor
VAELOR_02A.text: Truth? In your 'truth', she is cold dust beneath a churchyard stone! In here, she breathes! She smiles! She plays her song!

choices.text: She doesn't breathe, Vaelor. She repeats seven notes on a broken spring.

VAELOR_02B.speaker: Archillusionist Vaelor
VAELOR_02B.text: I tore down the laws of entropy! I forged an empire where no rose ever withers, where no child ever coughs blood into her pillow! Draw your blade, foster son! Let the curtain fall!

choices.text: [Draw Whisper and prepare for Phase 1]

VAELOR_02C.speaker: Archillusionist Vaelor
VAELOR_02C.text: The box... how did you... I threw those shards into the abyss the night you were banished. I couldn't bear to hear the lullaby... because it ended. Why won't you let me keep her safe?!

choices.text: Because she asked me to steal her away. It's time to let her rest.

VAELOR_BATTLE.speaker: Archillusionist Vaelor
VAELOR_BATTLE.text: Then let us see if your shadow can withstand the full glory of the dawn that never sets!

choices.text: [Begin Climactic Battle]

CYNTHIA_01.speaker: Lady Cynthia Vaelor [Spirit]
CYNTHIA_01.speakerTitle: The Soul in the Music Box
CYNTHIA_01.text: Hush now, Father. The music box has played its last turn. The sun has set, and the bed is warm. Master Voss... thank you for keeping your promise. The mirrors are quiet now. What will you do with my father's house?

choices.text: [ENDING A — True Dawn]: Release Cynthia, shatter the Heart, and let the fortress rest.
[ENDING B — Sovereign of Glass]: Claim the crown and rule the illusions yourself.
[ENDING C — Preserved Memory]: Seal the fortress in starlight amber as an eternal museum.
[ENDING D — Guild's Price]: Deliver the Heart of Mirrors to Sable for 3,000 moons.

ENDING_A.speaker: Lady Cynthia Vaelor [Spirit]
ENDING_A.speakerTitle: The Soul in the Music Box
ENDING_A.text: Look, Father... the sun is rising over the mountains. Warm sunlight... not glass. Goodbye, Kaelen.

choices.text: [Step out into the morning sun]

ENDING_B.speaker: Kaelen Voss
ENDING_B.text: The crown is mine. The midnight shall never end.

choices.text: [Ascend the glass throne]

ENDING_C.speaker: Lady Cynthia Vaelor [Spirit]
ENDING_C.speakerTitle: The Soul in the Music Box
ENDING_C.text: Frozen in amber... safe forever, yet never awake. Goodnight, Kaelen.

choices.text: [Turn the key and seal the doors]

ENDING_D.speaker: Guildmaster Sable
ENDING_D.text: A pleasure doing business with you, Shadowhand. The realm belongs to the syndicate now.

choices.text: [Count your silver moons]

MORVATH_01.speaker: Lord Morvath of the Silver Flagon
MORVATH_01.text: Sit, traveler! Drink of Duke Vaelor's vintage claret and taste the honeyed boar. For thirty years, this feast has warmed our hearts. Why march in the cold mountain winds when heaven is laid out before you?

choices.text: Look at your plate, Morvath. You are chewing cold fireplace ash.
[Truth Lens] Behold your wife's reflection in the silver cloche: she is starving to the bone.
A dream of joy cannot replace authentic life. Your sons did not die so you could hide here.

MORVATH_REBUT.speaker: Lord Morvath of the Silver Flagon
MORVATH_REBUT.text: Ash? If this is ash, why does it warm my soul? Outside these doors, my ancestral home burned and my sons were buried in mud. What virtue is there in gnawing cold stones of reality when a phantom roast brings peace?

choices.text: Peace built on an illusion is cowardice. True love honors the dead through truth.

MORVATH_REFUTE.speaker: Lord Morvath of the Silver Flagon
MORVATH_REFUTE.text: Vivienne... your hands... your ring has fallen into the dust! Merciful heavens... what have we done to ourselves?!

choices.text: Stand up, Morvath. Break the waltz and balance the scales.

MORVATH_SOLVED.speaker: Lord Morvath of the Silver Flagon
MORVATH_SOLVED.text: God forgive us... we have starved in heaven. Take the Tantalus Goblet, shadow-thief. Let the bitter air of reality flood this tomb!

choices.text: [Drop your silver fork and shatter the banquet glamour]

YGGDRA_01.speaker: Yggdra the Ancient Bough
YGGDRA_01.text: Mortal of flesh and shadow... Vaelor siphons my celestial sap into iron boilers. Three riddles of wood and steel bar your path. Answer true, or the thorny roots shall drag you into the loam.

choices.text: Speak your riddles, Ancient Father.
[Attack the thorny root barrier with your stiletto]

YGGDRA_R1.speaker: Yggdra the Ancient Bough
YGGDRA_R1.text: Riddle the First: I have no flesh, yet rings tell my mortal age. I drink starlight from the sky and hold the mountaintop in silent embrace. What am I?

choices.text: A Living Tree.
A Clockwork Escapement.

YGGDRA_R2.speaker: Yggdra the Ancient Bough
YGGDRA_R2.text: Truth speaks in your mouth. Riddle the Second: Cold as the grave, forged in fire, biting the bough to build the pyre. What breaks the wood?

choices.text: The Cold-Iron Ax.
The Phantom Mirror.

YGGDRA_R3.speaker: Yggdra the Ancient Bough
YGGDRA_R3.text: Riddle the Final: Woven in deepest darkness, linking every branch across the mountain crag. Invisible to the eye, yet sustaining all life. What binds us?

choices.text: The Harmonic Root-Weave.
The Chains of Lethe.

YGGDRA_FAIL.speaker: Yggdra the Ancient Bough
YGGDRA_FAIL.text: Falsehood! The thorns hunger for shadow-blood!

choices.text: [Defend yourself against the thorns!]

YGGDRA_SOLVED.speaker: Yggdra the Ancient Bough
YGGDRA_SOLVED.text: Wisdom dwells in your shadow. The iron siphons wither; the root-archway uncoils before you. Take the Starlight Dash, and leap across the void to the Spire!

choices.text: [Receive the blessing of the World Tree]

HAZEL_01.speaker: Mother Hazel
HAZEL_01.text: Come in, my handsome darling! Auntie Hazel has baked fresh hazelnut scones and poured piping-hot tea. Drink deep, and let Auntie tuck you into velvet slippers...

choices.text: [DEX 12 — Sleight of Hand]: Tip the drugged tea into the potted begonia and pretend to drink.
Who are all those porcelain dolls on your mantelpiece, Auntie?
I'm not your darling, witch. Step away from that hearth!

HAZEL_DOLLS.speaker: Mother Hazel
HAZEL_DOLLS.text: Aren't they my good children? They never bleed, they never yell, and they never, ever leave Auntie's hearth! Once you finish your tea, you shall have the prettiest little porcelain boots on the mantel...

choices.text: [DEX 12]: Divert her attention to the Chantilly lace and swap the tea for water.

HAZEL_SMOKE.speaker: Mother Hazel
HAZEL_SMOKE.text: Oh, that's my precious boy! Let the sweet slumber take you while Auntie prepares the sugar glaze... *[Kaelen secretly tosses volatile sulfur into the hearth fire!]*

choices.text: [The hearth detonates in purple sulfur smoke! Snip the apron key and grapple up the chimney flue!]

HAZEL_SOLVED.speaker: Mother Hazel
HAZEL_SOLVED.text: *COUGH! WHEEZE!* My lace doilies! You treacherous little gutter-rat! You locked the cupola hatch from outside! Give back my porcelain children!

choices.text: [Lock the miniature dollhouse door and claim the bone-sugar spoon]
